newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch shares recover late to end just firmer.
newsitem.headline: Dutch shares recover late to end just firmer.

text.p: Dutch shares finished the week marginally ahead on Friday after standing lower for much of a slow session only enlivened by some late action generated by April options expiry.
Dealers said the market was still bereft of direction with uncertainty over near-term U.S. interest rates keeping big investors on the sidelines and professionals nervous.

"The interest rate issue is still on everybody's mind and without fresh data we're stuck with low volumes," one said. The AEX index of 25 leading shares finished up 2.16 points, 0.29 percent, at 741.79.
Friday afternoon's expiry had, as expected, failed to deliver any real push, traders said, but did spark some trade.

The AEX index see-sawed narrowly around the 740 level in late dealings, one broker said options traders may have been defending index option positions expiring at that level by selling in the cash market.
The firmer Dow eventually helped the Dutch index settle above 740, previously a solid short-term resistance, he added.

Chemicals and pharmaceuticals group Akzo Nobel was the big loser among first tier Dutch stocks on Friday, hit by newspaper reports of a new trial firming up the link between low-dosage "mini-pill" oral contraceptives and increased risk of thrombosis.
The reports said laboratory tests confirmed earlier research indicating that the so-called third-generation pill doubled the chances of thrombosis.

Akzo unit Organon, manufacturer of top-selling mini-pill brands Mercilon and Marvelon, said earlier this year that consumer worries about the pill's health risks had cost it 70 million guilders in lost operating revenues in 1996.
"Well it is definitely a worry for the market," one dealer said. "Last time the issue came up it looked like it wouldn't be so bad for Akzo, but who knows how to take this."
Akzo shares traded as low as 256.50 guilders on the day, but ended down 5.70 guilders at 259.30.
Copier firm Oce-van der Grinten attracted some bottom fishers after a slid of over 16 guilders in the last two days triggered by first quarter results on Tuesday. Oce rose 5.40 guilders to 228.40.
Semiconductor equipment manufacturer ASM Lithography picked up 2.20 guilders to 148.20 after some positive broker comment.
